# About This Script

In this script we calculate the phylogenetic signal for every trait. We use parallel computing to measure the signal in each phylogenetic scenario, then measure mean and deviation. 

The output of this script is the Appendix S10 table with the phylogenetic signal of the ten functional traits evaluated among 79 terrestrial fern species from southern Brazilian Atlantic Forest.

> [!WARNING]
> The script demands a lot of memory and takes a minute to end. Therefore, clear garbage accumulated with `gc()`, the environment and restart the session. You may not be able to run this script if you have less than 8 GB of memory.

# Packages

```{r}
rm(list = ls())  # Clear the R environment
gc()             # Free up memory

# Load required libraries
library(caper)        # For comparative data and phylo.d
library(openxlsx)     # Read/write Excel files
library(readxl)       # Read Excel files
library(PVR)          # Phylogenetic eigenvectors
library(phytools)     # Phylogenetic tools (e.g., phylosig)
library(tidyverse)    # Tidyverse for data manipulation
library(foreach)      # Looping with parallel processing
library(doParallel)   # Backend for foreach (parallel computing)
library(here)            # To establish the path context

# Set reproducibility and options
set.seed(811)
options(scipen = 999)  # Prevent scientific notation
N = 1000                 # Number of trees (simulations)
```

# Load data

Now we will load the 1000 phylogenetic scenario, each scenario is slightly different from each other, due the insertion of 13 species at the genus root.

```{r}
mytrees <- read.tree(here("data/new_ftrees.txt"))[1:N] #Load 1000 trees
summary(is.ultrametric(mytrees))  # Check if trees are ultrametric
plot(mytrees[[1]])  # Plot the first tree

df <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = "t_matrix")  # Load trait data

# Remove node labels from all trees
mytrees2 <- list()  # Initialize empty list

for (i in seq_along(mytrees)) {
  mytrees2[[i]] <- mytrees[[i]]
  mytrees2[[i]]$node.label <- NULL
}
mytrees2 <- mytrees2[1:N]

# Filter out species not present in the tree
df <- filter(df, taxa %in% mytrees[[1]]$tip.label)

## Organize data to match species names between tree and trait data
org_traits <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %do%
  {
    df[match(mytrees2[[i]]$tip.label, df$taxa), ]
  }

# Check if species order matches in several examples
identical(org_traits[[2]]$taxa, mytrees[[2]]$tip.label)
identical(org_traits[[100]]$taxa, mytrees[[100]]$tip.label)
identical(org_traits[[414]]$taxa, mytrees[[918]]$tip.label)
identical(org_traits[[222]]$taxa, org_traits[[221]]$taxa)
```

# Do Parallel Computing

```{r}
no_cores <- detectCores() - 6  # Reserve 6 cores for the system
registerDoParallel(cores = no_cores)  # Register backend
cl <- makeCluster(no_cores, type = "FORK")  # Create parallel cluster
```

# K statistic (Blomberg’s K) for rhizome diameter (continuous trait)

K statistic is a procedure proposed by [Blomberg et al. (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0014-3820.2003.tb00285.x). Here we apply it for the 1000 phylogenetic scenario, extract the mean an it standard deviation.


```{r}
## Extract rhizome diameter for each tree/species combination
r_diam <-
  foreach(i = 1:N) %do%
  setNames(object = org_traits[[i]]$rhizome_diameter, nm = org_traits[[i]]$taxa)

# Calculate K statistic in parallel
K_diam <- foreach(i = 1:N, .combine = c, .verbose = T) %dopar%
  {
    phylosig(mytrees[[i]], r_diam[[i]], method = "K", nsim = 1000, test = T)$K
  }

# Extract associated p-values
K_diam_P <- foreach(i = 1:N, .combine = c, .verbose = T) %dopar%
  {
    phylosig(mytrees[[i]], r_diam[[i]], method = "K", nsim = 1000, test = T)$P
  }

# Combine K and p-values into a data frame
rhiz_diam <- cbind.data.frame(K = K_diam, pvalue = K_diam_P)

# Summary statistics for K
rhiz_diam_K <- data.frame(
  K = mean(rhiz_diam$K),
  min_K = min(rhiz_diam$K),
  max_K = max(rhiz_diam$K),
  sigs = sum(ifelse(rhiz_diam$pvalue <= 0.05, 1, 0) / 1000)
)

```

# D Statistic for the binary traits

D statistic is a procedure proposed by [Fritz & Purvis (2010)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1523-1739.2010.01455.x). Here we apply it for the 1000 phylogenetic scenario, extract the mean and its standard deviation.

For knowledge, six categorical traits were split into binary.

```{r}
## Function to create comparative data objects for each tree
comp_dat <- function(x, y) {
  for (i in seq_along(mytrees2)) {
    y[[i]] <- comparative.data(mytrees2[[i]], x, names.col = "species")
  }
  return(y)
}

## Function to run phylo.d in parallel
phy_d <- function(x) {
  foreach(i = seq_along(mytrees2)) %dopar%
    {
      phylo.d(x[[i]], binvar = trait)
    }
}

## Function to convert phylo.d output to a data frame
d_df <- function(x, y) {
  for (i in seq_along(mytrees2)) {
    y[i, 1] <- x[[i]]$DEstimate
    y[i, 2] <- x[[i]]$Pval1
    y[i, 3] <- x[[i]]$Pval0
  }
  colnames(y) <- c("D", "P1", "P0")
  return(y)
}
```

## Rhizome type 

```{r}
gc()
# Create binary trait tables for each rhizome type
rhiz_type2 <- table(
  names = org_traits[[1]]$taxa,
  trait = org_traits[[1]]$rhizome_type
)

rhiz_comp <- data.frame(
  species = rownames(rhiz_type2),
  trait = rhiz_type2[, "Compact"],
  row.names = NULL
)

rhiz_crep <- data.frame(
  species = rownames(rhiz_type2),
  trait = rhiz_type2[, "Short-Creeping"],
  row.names = NULL
)

rhiz_lrep <- data.frame(
  species = rownames(rhiz_type2),
  trait = rhiz_type2[, "Long-Creeping"],
  row.names = NULL
)


##Empty objects to insert values

list_emp <- vector(mode = "list", length = length(mytrees2))
matr_emp <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(mytrees2), ncol = 3)

rhiz_comp_D <- comp_dat(x = rhiz_comp, y = list_emp) %>%
  phy_d() %>%
  d_df(y = matr_emp)

rhiz_cr_D <- comp_dat(x = rhiz_crep, y = list_emp) %>%
  phy_d() %>%
  d_df(y = matr_emp)

rhiz_lr_D <- comp_dat(x = rhiz_lrep, y = list_emp) %>%
  phy_d() %>%
  d_df(y = matr_emp)

mean(rhiz_comp_D[, 1])
mean(rhiz_cr_D[, 1])
```

## Multipinnate laminae

```{r}
  row.names = NULL
) # multipinnate laminae (from 2:n)

lam_mult_D <- comp_dat(x = lam_mult, y = list_emp) %>%
  phy_d() %>%
  d_df(y = matr_emp)

mean(lam_mult_D[, 1])
```

## Indusium

For knowledge, pseudo-indusium (some pteridoids) was considered indusium since it has an analogous function.

```{r}
gc()

indu <- data.frame(species = df$taxa, trait = df$indusium, row.names = NULL)
indu_D <- comp_dat(x = indu, y = list_emp) %>% phy_d() %>% d_df(y = matr_emp)
```


# Outputting data (Appendix S10)

The output of this analysis is a summary of phylogenetic signal.

```{r}
# Create a list of D statistics
D_list <- vector(mode = "list")
D_list[[1]] <- rhiz_comp_D
D_list[[2]] <- rhiz_cr_D
D_list[[3]] <- rhiz_lr_D
D_list[[4]] <- lam_mult_D
D_list[[5]] <- lam_dim_D
D_list[[6]] <- lam_tri_D
D_list[[7]] <- buds_D
D_list[[8]] <- indu_D
D_list[[9]] <- chl_D


## Function to summarise all data
count <- function(x) {
  D <- capture.output(cat(
    round(mean(x[, 1]), 2),
    "[",
    round(range(x[, 1]), 2),
    "]"
  ))
  P0 <- length(which(x[, 3] <= 0.05))
  P1 <- length(which(x[, 2] <= 0.05))
  vec <- rbind(D, P0, P1)

  return(vec)
}
names <- c(
  'riz_comp',
  "riz_cr",
  "riz_lr",
  "lam_mult",
  "lam_dim",
  "lam_tri",
  "buds",
  "ind",
  'chl'
)

## Summarising all
D_matrix <- foreach(i = seq_along(D_list), .combine = cbind) %do%
  {
    count(D_list[[i]])
  }

rownames(D_matrix) <- c("D", "P0", "P1")
colnames(D_matrix) <- names

## Add Bloomberg K in the raw list
D_list[[11]] <- rhiz_diam
```

# Save data

```{r}
write.xlsx(list(D = D_matrix, K = rhiz_diam_K), file = here( "outputs/phylo_sig.xlsx"))

### Save raw data
saveRDS(D_list, file = here("outputs/phylo_sig_result.RDS"))

D_list <- readRDS(here("outputs/phylo_sig_result.RDS"))
```
